tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. The most likely reason is that ships ring the harbour from January 1780, and the dated frames run on into 1781, so the town looks cut off by sea. There is also an enemy camp or fields on the land side. I see no food, no starving people and no text about hunger.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of many ships arrives from the sea in frames 47-52 (Jan–Oct 1780). I can't tell whose ships they are or whether they bring supplies. This could be a relief fleet or an attacking one, and the pictures don't settle it.
